# DESIGN.md — design learnings from mass-creating Apple Shortcuts automations

**Assisted-by: Hermes Agent · GLM 5.3 Flash <hermes-ollamacloud-glm53flash@local>** (generated by `agent-detect trailer assisted-by`)

This document records everything we learned driving macOS Apple Shortcuts
through an AI agent to mass-create 288 time-of-day Automations. The live
session: 69 automations existed (00:00–05:40), 219 were created, 5
duplicates were deleted, 1 wrong-interval automation (23:30) was fixed,
and the final state was verified 288/288 slots, 0 duplicates, 0 gaps.
Total machine time ≈ 70 minutes.

## 1. The core problem

Apple Shortcuts has **no scripting interface for Automations**:

- The AppleScript dictionary only exposes *running* shortcuts
  (`run shortcut`), not the Automation triggers.
- The Automations database is in a TCC-protected group container that
  background processes cannot read.
- Therefore the GUI **is** the API. Everything below is about making GUI
  automation *reliable* rather than fighting it blind.

## 2. Architecture of the working pipeline

```
schedule generation (Python)
  → per-item AppleScript (osascript .scpt files)
      ├─ keyboard: ⌥⌘N (New Automation), ↓+Enter (Time of Day),
      │   typing the time, Enter to submit forms
      ├─ AX actions: AXPress on radio buttons, confirm-dialog buttons
      ├─ CGEvent true mouse events: ONLY for the time-picker hour field
      │   and the shortcut picker card grid (SwiftUI internals)
      └─ AX tree dumps after every step (state verification)
  → verification loop
      ├─ PyObjC AXOutline walk = full ordered list read (all 288 rows)
      ├─ local OCR (Swift + Apple Vision) for pixel truth
      ├─ multimodal vision for human-level sanity checks
      └─ sidebar badge count as ground truth
```

Per-item cost: ~18s with conservative delays, ~11s with tuned delays.
Reliability at tuned delays: ~99% (2 misfires in 219 creates; both
caught by audit and fixed).

## 3. Coordinate spaces (the #1 time sink)

- **Screenshot pixels ≠ native points.** Retina captures are ~1.28× the
  native coordinate space. Clicking vision-estimated screenshot pixels
  as native coordinates lands ~80px off. Never do it.
- **`computer_use` coordinate delivery** silently remapped a click
  (reported clicking (798, 714.5) when asked for (818, 527)). Its
  element-index clicks are fine; raw coordinates are not trustworthy
  here.
- **System Events `click at` is a trap**: on SwiftUI elements it presses
  the element's *activation point*, not the coordinates you gave it.
  It is not a coordinate click.
- **User-parked-mouse calibration is gold.** Have the user park the
  mouse over each target and read the exact cursor position
  (`CGEventGetLocation` via JXA) — those numbers are ground truth.
  Use them once to *derive element selectors* (via element-at-point),
  then act through selectors/keyboard forever after.

## 4. What works, per control type

| Control | Technique that works | Technique that fails |
|---|---|---|
| Menu-bar actions (New Automation) | `⌥⌘N` hotkey | clicking the `+` button |
| Trigger list (Time of Day) | ↓ arrow once + Enter | blind arrow spam |
| Time picker hour field | **CGEvent true click** at calibrated point, then type `hh`, RIGHT, `mm`, RIGHT, `a`/`p` | Tab (never reaches it), arrows (ignored), AXPress increment/decrement (accepted but no-op), `click at` (activates wrong control) |
| Run Immediately radio | `perform action "AXPress"` | CGEvent click at AX-derived center (hot zone mismatch), `set focused` + typing |
| Footer wizard buttons (Back/Next/Done) | **Enter submits the form** (basic form UX — use it!) | AXPress (ignored — SwiftUI), `click at` (activation point ≠ button) |
| Shortcut picker cards | CGEvent click at calibrated card centers | AXPress, `click at` |
| Confirm dialogs ("Delete automation?") | **AXPress the named button** (`whose description is "Delete"`) | Return (**Cancel is the default button** — Return cancels!), Tab+Return (unreliable) |
| List row deletion | AX `set AXSelected` on the row, then ⌘Delete, then AXPress Delete in dialog | Delete key alone (opens the row editor) |

The pattern: **AppKit controls honor AXPress; SwiftUI internals honor
true CGEvent mouse events only.** Keyboard goes where the form's default
button goes — which is why Enter both advances the wizard and cancels
destructive confirm dialogs.

## 5. Verification is the whole game

- **AX tree dumps after every step.** Fingerprints, not vibes: the When
  sheet has "Repeat" + "Daily" popup; the picker sheet's title is
  `At <time>, daily`; the trigger list has Time of Day/Alarm rows.
- **Read the focused element after every keystroke**
  (`AXFocusedUIElement` role/value). Keystrokes that "didn't take" are
  usually focus sitting somewhere unexpected.
- **AXPress sets values, not focus.** Pressing a radio selects it but
  keyboard focus stays put — a later Tab then moves focus from wherever
  it really was, leaking keystrokes into other controls. This caused
  our "Daily got selected" bug.
- **Vision LLM misreads small text** (read "5:35" as "5:05", missed
  "4:44"→"5:44" edits). Treat vision as a rough check. For
  deterministic reads, build a **local OCR tool**: Swift + Apple's
  Vision framework (`VNRecognizeTextRequest`), ~68KB binary, instant,
  conf=1.00 on UI text.
- **The sidebar badge is ground truth for counts.** The automation list
  is virtualized: AX reads can return offscreen rows, stale rows after
  re-renders, and double-captured rows at scroll boundaries. Badge lags
  by a refresh, but it never double-counts.
- **Duplicates in a sorted list = adjacent identical rows.** Check
  adjacency, not presence — reader artifacts duplicate non-adjacent
  phantom pairs.

## 6. Tooling notes

- **AppleScript under System Events hits terminology clashes**
  (`outline`, `row`, `scroll area` as bare class names in `-e` one-liners
  and even .scpt files depending on context). Compile errors like
  "Expected end of line but found class name" mean: move to PyObjC.
- **PyObjC (modern, 12.x) returns out-params as tuples** —
  `AXUIElementCopyElementAtPosition` → `(err, element)`. JXA
  (`osascript -l JavaScript`) cannot read those out-params at all
  (returns `undefined`); System Events UI scripting is the fallback, not
  the primary.
- **Write AppleScript to `.scpt` files**, never inline `-e` for anything
  with tell-blocks, handlers, or `entire contents`.
- **`uv venv` + `uv pip install pyobjc-framework-ApplicationServices`**
  (PEP 668 blocks system pip; uv's quick `--with` resolution missed the
  framework chain).
- CGEvent posting from Python needs no extra deps beyond PyObjC-Quartz:
  move → mouseDown (0.08–0.12s) → mouseUp. Set `kCGMouseEventClickState`.

## 7. Session orchestration nifties

- **START/FINISH `display dialog` alerts bracket every automated run.**
  The user must know when the machine is agent-driven. `display
  notification` is silent (never seen in practice) — use dialogs. The
  dialog steals frontmost, so re-activate the target app after it.
- **Frontmost gating**: never send keystrokes unless the target app is
  frontmost; the agent's own dialogs and chat can eat them otherwise.
  One stray Tab/Return typed into the chat composer proves the point.
- **Self-healing batch runner**: on a stale sheet, fire one Escape and
  continue instead of failing the run; retry each item once; log every
  result line; recompute "what's missing" from the live list rather than
  trusting the log.
- **Schedule-driven, not code-driven**: a plain-text schedule file
  (`HH MM cardX cardY am/pm` per line) makes the batch resumable from
  any line and auditable.
- **Interval→card mapping** for the 5-minute grid: :00→Every Hour,
  :15/:45→Every Quarter Hour, :30→Every Half Hour, others→Every 5
  minutes. Keep a saved card-position map (row 1: x=476/630/784 at
  y=728; row 2 col 1 at y=834) — but re-derive by dump when the sheet
  moves.
- **Delays: tune down only after a clean full pass.** 1s pacing during
  recipe discovery, ~0.35–0.9s once proven. Speed without verification
  just manufactures duplicates to clean up later.
- **Background-process timeouts kill GUI batches**: a 10-min wrapper
  timeout SIGTERMed a 60-min run mid-flight (exit 143). For Hermes:
  foreground with generous timeouts, or chunked background runs.
- **Interleaved failures produce stragglers + duplicates** (retries
  after partial sheet states). Budget an audit+dedupe pass at the end;
  it found 5 dups and 1 wrong interval out of 219 creates.

## 8. User-in-the-loop rules that made this work

These came from the human steering the session and are non-negotiable:

1. **Zero blind coordinate clicks.** Hover coordinates are probes for
   element discovery; act via selectors or keyboard.
2. **Vision-confirm every step of a new flow** before batching it.
3. **START and FINISH alerts** around every automated action, so the
   user knows when not to touch the machine.
4. **Hand control back early** when stuck rather than grinding.
5. **Never fabricate a verification.** If the screenshot can't be read,
   say so and use AX/OCR instead.

## 9. What we'd build next

- Extract the working `.scpt` + PyObjC recipes into a small CLI
  (`ascr-automation`) so the batch is a script, not a session artifact.
- An AX-native time-picker setter if Apple ever exposes one (check each
  macOS release; `increment`/`decrement` custom actions exist but are
  no-ops today).
- A `--verify` mode that produces the full 288-slot audit report as its
  output artifact.
